statement: A Euclidean vector (or simply vector) is a geometric object that possesses both magnitude (or length) and direction, commonly depicted as a directed line segment or arrow connecting an initial point $A$ to a terminal point $B$, which can be added together and scaled by numbers (scalars) to form a vector space satisfying vector axioms.

symbols.meaning: Length, magnitude, or Euclidean norm of vector \mathbf{a}
Normalized unit vector pointing in the direction of \mathbf{a}
Zero vector with length zero and indeterminate direction
Scalar components of vector \mathbf{a} in an orthonormal basis
Unit vector perpendicular to vectors \mathbf{a} and \mathbf{b} completing a right-handed system

properties.property: The length (Euclidean norm) of vector \mathbf{a} is given by \|\mathbf{a}\| = \sqrt{a_1^2 + a_2^2 + a_3^2} = \sqrt{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{a}}.
properties.why: it is a consequence of the Pythagorean theorem since basis vectors are orthogonal unit vectors

properties.property: Any non-zero vector \mathbf{a} can be normalized into a unit vector of length one by scaling by the reciprocal of its length: \mathbf{\hat{a}} = \frac{\mathbf{a}}{\|\mathbf{a}\|} = \frac{a_1}{\|\mathbf{a}\|}\mathbf{e}_1 + \frac{a_2}{\|\mathbf{a}\|}\mathbf{e}_2 + \frac{a_3}{\|\mathbf{a}\|}\mathbf{e}_3.
properties.why: scaling a vector by the reciprocal of its length scales its magnitude to one while preserving direction

properties.property: The zero vector \mathbf{0} = (0, 0, 0) has length zero, satisfies \mathbf{0} + \mathbf{a} = \mathbf{a} for all \mathbf{a}, has an indeterminate direction, and cannot be normalized.
properties.why: there exists no unit vector that is a scalar multiple of the zero vector

properties.property: Scalar multiplication distributes over vector addition such that r(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}) = r\mathbf{a} + r\mathbf{b}, with negative scalars flipping vector direction by 180° such that \mathbf{a} - \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{a} + (-1)\mathbf{b}.
properties.why: Euclidean vectors satisfy the vector space axioms under addition and scaling

properties.property: The dot product of two vectors is a scalar defined geometrically as \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = \|\mathbf{a}\| \|\mathbf{b}\| \cos\theta and componentwise as \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = a_1 b_1 + a_2 b_2 + a_3 b_3.
properties.why: it multiplies the magnitude of \mathbf{a} by the length of the directional component of \mathbf{b} along \mathbf{a}

properties.property: The cross product \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} in three dimensions is a vector perpendicular to both \mathbf{a} and \mathbf{b} defined as \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \|\mathbf{a}\| \|\mathbf{b}\| \sin(\theta)\,\mathbf{n} = (a_2 b_3 - a_3 b_2)\mathbf{e}_1 + (a_3 b_1 - a_1 b_3)\mathbf{e}_2 + (a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1)\mathbf{e}_3.
properties.why: it forms a right-handed system whose magnitude corresponds to the area of the parallelogram spanned by \mathbf{a} and \mathbf{b}

properties.property: The scalar triple product (\mathbf{a}\ \mathbf{b}\ \mathbf{c}) = \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) equals the determinant of the 3-by-3 matrix formed by the row vectors, is alternating under pairwise swaps, and its absolute value is the volume of the spanned parallelepiped.
properties.why: it is zero if and only if the three vectors are linearly dependent (coplanar)

properties.property: A vector \mathbf{a} is invariant under conversion between multiple Cartesian orthonormal bases (e.g., \mathbf{a} = \sum p_i \mathbf{e}_i = \sum u_i \mathbf{n}_i), where components in any orthonormal basis are given by projections p_i = \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{e}_i and u_i = \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{n}_i.
properties.why: the vector geometric object exists independently of the coordinate basis chosen to represent it

assumptions.assumption: The coordinate basis vectors \mathbf{e}_1, \mathbf{e}_2, \mathbf{e}_3 are orthonormal.
assumptions.breaks_when: The basis vectors are non-orthogonal or non-unit length, which causes the Pythagorean component formula for norm and componentwise dot product to fail.

assumptions.assumption: Space is three-dimensional and equipped with a standard right-handed orientation.
assumptions.breaks_when: The dimension is not 3 (or 7) where cross products are not defined as vectors, or a left-handed orientation is used where cross products produce pseudovectors.

assumptions.assumption: Vectors subjected to normalization have non-zero length (\|\mathbf{a}\| > 0).
assumptions.breaks_when: The vector is the zero vector \mathbf{0}, causing division by zero.

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero / undefined unit vector \mathbf{\hat{a}}
failure_modes.cause: The zero vector has length zero and indeterminate direction; no unit vector is a multiple of the zero vector.

failure_modes.mode: Cross product dimensionality and chirality failure
failure_modes.signature: Undefined operation or sign inversion / pseudovector behavior
failure_modes.cause: Cross product is only meaningful in three or seven dimensions and requires a right-handed system convention.

failure_modes.mode: Coplanar degeneration of scalar triple product
failure_modes.cause: The three vectors are linearly dependent and lie in the same plane, causing the spanned volume to collapse to zero.
